correctness.rationale: Summing the Fourier multiplier over the matrix Y enforces B+CX+XC=0. The trace-adjoint identity makes A lie in the image of S_C; the resulting affine fibre sum has magnitude \(q^{n^2+\nu(C)}\) and the stated phase. The matrix Hom classification gives nu(C) as the f versus f-minus partition pairing; dividing general-linear-group order by centralizers yields the coupled primary-orbit product. The n=2 trace/determinant strata, extreme singular values, and finite-field polynomial density bounds are reconstructed in RESULT.md. A standalone checker independently reproduces the q=2,3,4 two-dimensional kernel histograms and direct Fourier sums in q=2,3, and exhausts q=2,3 dimension-three kernel histograms. Finite checks support, rather than establish, the universal claim.

value.rationale: The Jordan-product graph is a natural nonlinear subvariety of three full matrix spaces. Its exact convolution singular spectrum and sharp pseudoinverse condition numbers reveal a qualitative Fourier-support transition: for each fixed n the support density tends to 1 along odd fields but 0 along fields of characteristic two. The coupled negative-primary classification is necessary for the complete all-dimension spectral census, and ordinary anticommuting pair counts do not determine it. The object/invariant are independently motivated by additive harmonic analysis and Jordan multiplication; the finding is not an arbitrary isolated parameter calculation.
